title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Ten nearby corridors and micro-districts, each paired with one practical, directly sourced reason to go.

cards.title: Start at the Rail Gateway
cards.subtitle: For regional and intercity connections
cards.notes: Walk east on Market Street when you need the campus-side approach to 30th Street Station; use marked crossings and the signed station entrance.
cards.short_summary: A transportation-focused block at University City’s eastern edge.
cards.evidence_claim: The 30th Street district provides access to William H. Gray III 30th Street Station and is planned as a gateway with river and park connections.
cards.access_notes: Active transportation district; follow station rules and use designated crossings and entrances.

cards.title: Follow the Athletics Approach
cards.subtitle: For the route toward Vidas
cards.notes: Trace the university’s published walking approach along Lancaster and Powelton avenues when heading toward the Vidas Athletic Complex.
cards.short_summary: A westbound corridor linking the main campus orbit with Drexel athletics.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel directs pedestrians toward the Vidas Athletic Complex via Lancaster Avenue and Powelton Avenue.
cards.access_notes: The cited directions establish the route, not present sidewalk conditions or travel time.

cards.title: Catch the Dollar Stroll Corridor
cards.subtitle: For a recurring neighborhood event
cards.notes: Check the event date before traveling southwest, then use the organizer’s current map to see which corridor vendors are participating.
cards.short_summary: A long commercial stretch used for the seasonal Baltimore Avenue Dollar Stroll.
cards.evidence_claim: University City District identifies Baltimore Avenue from 40th to 51st streets as the commercial corridor for its recurring Dollar Stroll.
cards.access_notes: The event is seasonal; participation, dates, and individual offers can change.

cards.entity_name: Schuylkill River Trail access near Market and Chestnut streets
cards.title: Join the River Trail
cards.subtitle: For a mapped cycling connection
cards.notes: Use the city bicycle map to locate the bridge approaches, and follow its instruction to walk your bicycle on the access ramp.
cards.short_summary: The nearest mapped bridge approaches into the riverfront trail network.
cards.evidence_claim: Philadelphia’s bicycle map marks Schuylkill River Trail access from the Market and Chestnut Street bridges near University City.
cards.access_notes: The map instructs cyclists to walk bicycles on the bridge access ramp; check separately for closures.

cards.title: Walk the Public-Art District
cards.subtitle: For murals and outdoor installations
cards.notes: Enter the district east of campus and use its experience guide to connect Mural Row, the Highline Park sculpture, and other outdoor works.
cards.short_summary: A campus-adjacent development district with a documented public-art network.
cards.evidence_claim: Schuylkill Yards documents a district public-art collection that includes Mural Row, a sculpture at Highline Park, and a mural by David Guinn.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor works and public spaces may be affected by construction or scheduled events.

cards.title: See the Mixed-Use Science District
cards.subtitle: For its combination of spaces
cards.notes: Walk west along Market Street to examine how laboratories and offices sit alongside housing, retail, community uses, and green space.
cards.short_summary: A nearby mixed-use district organized around science and community space.
cards.evidence_claim: uCity Square describes its district as containing laboratory, clinical, office, retail, residential, community, and green spaces.
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor circulation does not imply access to private laboratories, offices, or residences.

cards.title: Use the Completed Protected Lane
cards.subtitle: For an eastbound bicycle corridor
cards.notes: Choose this stretch for an eastbound ride, stay within the parking-protected lane, and watch signals and turning movements at intersections.
cards.short_summary: A completed parking-protected bicycle segment running through University City.
cards.evidence_claim: Philadelphia lists the Chestnut Street parking-protected bicycle lane from 33rd to 45th streets as completed.
cards.access_notes: Street infrastructure remains subject to maintenance, construction, and temporary traffic controls.

cards.title: Browse a Multi-Block Retail Spine
cards.subtitle: For varied storefronts between transit stops
cards.notes: Walk the blocks between the Market–Frankford Line and trolley portal to survey the corridor’s mix of shops, books, services, and food.
cards.short_summary: A compact commercial spine bracketed by rapid-transit and trolley access.
cards.evidence_claim: University City District describes the 40th Street corridor as several commercial blocks between an elevated-train stop and a trolley station, with varied shops and dining.
cards.source_title: A Look at the Old-Timers on University City's Vibrant 40th Street Corridor
cards.access_notes: Individual storefront access and operating hours vary; consult each destination directly.

cards.title: Read a Corridor in Transition
cards.subtitle: For an active Complete Streets project
cards.notes: Review the city project page before visiting, then look for the planned bikeway, crossing, landscaping, lighting, and signal improvements.
cards.short_summary: A southwest University City corridor undergoing a phased multimodal redesign.
cards.evidence_claim: Philadelphia’s Woodland Avenue project includes a raised two-way bikeway, new signals and crosswalks, trees, landscaping, and street lighting between the VA driveway and 42nd Street.
cards.source_title: Woodland Avenue Complete Streets Project (VA Driveway to 42nd Street)
cards.access_notes: The project is phased and remains in progress; current conditions may differ from the final design.

cards.title: Take the Westbound Bike Counterpart
cards.subtitle: For a separated cross-city route
cards.notes: Use Walnut for the westbound leg of a bike trip, remaining alert to posted controls at intersections and any unfinished or repaired segments.
cards.short_summary: A westbound separated bicycle corridor paired with Chestnut Street’s eastbound lane.
cards.evidence_claim: Philadelphia identifies the Walnut Street separated bicycle lane from 33rd to 63rd streets as a westbound counterpart to the eastbound Chestnut Street lane.
cards.source_title: City Celebrates Bicycle Safety Month by Launching Visual Recap of 2023 Bicycle Network Changes
cards.access_notes: Follow current signs, signals, construction controls, and ordinary street-use rules.
